failure_summary.description: Ready domain actions or required cache-result saves were omitted.
Agents re-searched instead of refining cached results, or processed unchanged domains and unrequested proximity.
Explicit solo or group traveler counts were omitted from hotel searches.
Round-trip legs were combined, or a missing flight origin was guessed rather than requested.
Agents imported runtime helpers or manipulated results in Python instead of using the provided tools.

patch.reasoning: The skill already requires saving tool results, using runtime tools without imports, and keeping work scoped, so those rules need no duplication. These edits make two recurring gaps explicit: passing stated traveler counts to hotel calls and using domain filter tools rather than Python-side filtering. A short flight rule reinforces separate directional legs and prevents guessing a missing endpoint.

edits.target: - Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters; do not infer amenities, ratings, or other preferences. Do not infer exact party or room counts from broad descriptions such as “family.” Treat “solo” as one traveler only when a supported traveler-count field is available; do not infer a room count from it. A traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one.
edits.content: - Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters; do not infer amenities, ratings, or other preferences. For hotel calls, include every explicitly stated traveler count as `num_people` when supported (for example, `solo` means `num_people=1`). Do not infer counts from broad descriptions such as “family,” or infer `num_rooms` from a traveler count; include room count only when explicitly stated. A traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one.

edits.target: - When refining a cached result, do not resend criteria already represented in that result; apply the newly introduced preference with the appropriate filter.
edits.content: - When refining a cached result, use the domain’s filter tool on a compatible cached result; do not implement filtering by iterating over or editing result objects in Python. Do not resend criteria already represented in that result; apply the newly introduced preference with the appropriate filter.

- For round trips, never encode outbound and return legs as two dates in one call: make a separate directional search for each leg. Do not assume the origin is the stated destination; if a required endpoint is missing, seek it rather than guessing.
